what: How the exclusion rate of the email synth pool against its own generator-held-out target set (heldout/synth-email-v2) is read.

measure.rate: decontamination.excluded_total / the candidates scanned (manifest rows_too_short_by_set.synth-candidates.rows), from pool/synth-email-v1/manifest.json
measure.also_reported: the rate per class (excluded_by_target ids mapped to their stratum), and the targets checkable at n=8 (rows minus too_short)

fixed.note: Rule 2: neither moves to change how the rate reads.

bands.reading: The template partition yields held-out emails whose text no training row contains at 0.5 of 8-grams. Read with the scan's positive control (synth::tests::a_held_out_target_is_its_rows_content_so_the_scan_still_tells_rows_apart): without it, 0 is indistinguishable from a scan that cannot hit.
Shared slot fillers make a few training rows near-copies of a held-out email; the partition holds and the scan removed them, as designed. The held-out set stands as a test of unseen templates.

Substantial overlap through shared fillers and phrasing: the partition is weak. The pool may train (the excluded rows are gone), but email held-out scores partly measure phrasing seen in training; a gap is recorded and partitioning the filler vocabulary as well as the templates goes to the advisor before email held-out numbers are used.
The template partition does not separate the text. Email held-out results are not admitted as evidence of generalization until the generator partitions content, not only templates.
The target-text defect persists or another scaffolding path exists; the fix is wrong.

per_class: Any class whose own rate passes 0.5 is named, whatever the overall band.
